questions.stem: How do the melting points of transition metals compare to those of Group 1 metals?

options.text: Transition metals have much lower melting points
Transition metals have much higher melting points
It depends on the specific element

questions.explanation: Transition metals have much higher melting points than Group 1 metals. For example, iron melts at 1538 degrees C while sodium melts at just 98 degrees C. Transition metals are also harder, denser, and stronger than Group 1 metals.

questions.stem: What colour are Fe³⁺ ions in solution?
questions.explanation: Fe³⁺ ions produce yellow or brown solutions. This is different from Fe²⁺ ions, which produce pale green solutions. The ability of iron to form two different ions (Fe²⁺ and Fe³⁺) is an example of the variable oxidation states characteristic of transition metals.
